14-069.r: MF band → not used in INSAT/GSAT satellite communication; bands used in India: S, C, Upper Extended C, Ku and Ka.

14-070.r: Television transmission → simplex communication: one-way only, information travels in one direction.

14-071.r: India's first remote sensing satellite IRS-1A → launched 17 March 1988 from Baikonur Cosmodrome, Soviet Union.

14-072.r: IRS (Indian Remote Sensing) satellites → used for crop productivity, locating groundwater, mineral exploration; not telecommunications or traffic studies.

14-073.r: Satellite/remote sensing data estimate → chlorophyll in vegetation, greenhouse gas from rice paddies, land surface temperature → all three.

14-074.r: INSAT-3C → launched by Arianespace's Ariane-4 from Kourou, French Guiana (South America).

14-075.r: 22 December 2005 → ISRO launched INSAT-4A (first of INSAT-4 series, 3081 kg) from Kourou, French Guiana, on an Ariane-5 vehicle.

14-076.r: PSLV-C37 (39th PSLV flight, 15 February 2017) → 104 satellites in one flight: Cartosat-2 series plus 103 co-passengers, total 1378 kg, from Sriharikota.

14-078.r: Last PSLV mission of 2022 → PSLV-C54/EOS-06, launched 26 November 2022 from Sriharikota.

14-079.r: Chandrayaan-3 → 14 July 2023 (LVM3-M4); Aditya-L1 → 2 September 2023 (PSLV-C57); INSAT-3DS → 17 February 2024 (GSLV-F14); RLV-LEX-01 → 2 April 2023.

14-080.r: PSLV-C55 (57th PSLV mission) → launched TeLEOS-2 (primary) and Lumelite-4 on 22 April 2023 from Sriharikota; commercial mission through NSIL.

14-081.r: XPoSat (X-ray Polarimeter Satellite, PSLV-C58, 1 January 2024) → India's first dedicated polarimetry mission for bright X-ray sources; two payloads in low earth orbit → both true.

14-082.r: POEM-4 (PSLV Orbital Experimental Module) → controlled re-entry, hit Indian Ocean on 4 April 2025; part of PSLV-C60/SpaDeX mission (launched 30 December 2024).

14-083.r: Chronological order: SITE (1975, NASA–ISRO) → STEP (1977) → APPLE (19 June 1981) → IGMD programme (DRDO, 1983).
14-083.h: S-S-A-I: two satellite experiments (SITE, STEP), then APPLE, then missiles.

14-084.r: APPLE (Ariane Passenger Payload Experiment) → India's first experimental geostationary communication satellite; launched 19 June 1981 by Ariane from Kourou, French Guiana.

14-086.r: INSAT-1D → launched 12 June 1990; multipurpose satellite for telephone, television and weather observation.
14-086.t: Options differ only by day (10, 12, 13, 15 June 1990): it is the 12th.

14-087.r: INSAT-2A → launched 10 July 1992 from Kourou, French Guiana.
14-087.c: The book calls INSAT-2A India's first indigenously built satellite; Aryabhatta (April 19th, 1975, an option here) was built in India earlier. INSAT-2A was the first home-built INSAT.

14-088.r: INSAT-4C (2168 kg, Rs. 350 crore) → lost when its GSLV exploded 60 seconds after lift-off, 10 July 2006; heaviest ISRO satellite now GSAT-11 (5854 kg).

14-089.r: IRNSS-1A, India's first dedicated navigation satellite → launched by PSLV-C22 on 1 July 2013 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

14-090.r: IRNSS (NavIC = Navigation with Indian Constellation) → seven satellites: three geostationary, four geosynchronous; covers India and 1500 km around (not 5500 sq. km); regional, not global.

14-092.r: GSLV-F15 (29 January 2025) → carried NVS-02 navigation satellite; ISRO's 100th launch from Sriharikota; 17th GSLV flight → more than one option true.

14-093.r: Own satellite navigation: global → GPS (USA), GLONASS (Russia), Galileo (EU), BeiDou (China); regional → NavIC (India), QZSS/Michibiki (Japan).

14-094.r: Galileo → European Union's global multi-satellite navigation system (through ESA), live in 2016; civilian-controlled, inter-operable with GPS and GLONASS.

14-095.r: GPS = Global Positioning System → space-based navigation system by the U.S. Department of Defence; fully operational from 27 April 1995.

14-096.r: GPS technology is used in → mobile phone operations, banking (precise timing) and controlling power grids → all three.

14-097.r: GAGAN (ISRO + Airports Authority of India) → satellite-based augmentation system; extra accuracy and integrity, uniform air traffic management; benefits not limited to aviation.

14-098.r: Launch vehicle order: SLV (10 August 1979) → ASLV (24 March 1987) → PSLV (20 September 1993) → GSLV (18 April 2001).
14-098.h: S-A-P-G: SLV, Augmented, Polar, Geosynchronous; vehicles grow in size.

14-099.r: SLV-3 → Rohini (RS-1, 18 July 1980); ASLV → SROSS-C; PSLV → Chandrayaan-1; GSLV → EDUSAT.

14-100.r: ISRO → Bengaluru; IIRS → Dehradun; NRSA (now NRSC) → Hyderabad; SAC (Space Applications Centre) → Ahmedabad.

14-101.r: ISRO Master Control Facility → Hassan, Karnataka (set up 1982) to control geostationary and geosynchronous satellites; another MCF at Bhopal (2005).

14-102.r: ISRO → Bengaluru; IUCA (astronomy and astrophysics) → Pune; IUAC (accelerator centre) → New Delhi; VSSC → Thiruvananthapuram.
14-102.t: Don't mix IUCA (Pune, astronomy) with IUAC (New Delhi, accelerator).

14-103.r: Wrong pair: ISRO Satellite Centre – Sriharikota; it is at Bengaluru (set up 1972 as ISSP; renamed UR Rao Satellite Centre in 2018). Other pairs correct.

14-104.r: Correct pair: Space Applications Centre – Ahmedabad. ISRO Satellite Centre (URSC) → Bengaluru; VSSC → Thiruvananthapuram; SHAR Centre → Sriharikota.

14-105.r: Correct: VSSC → Trivandrum; URSC → Bengaluru. Swapped: NRSC → Hyderabad (not Dehradun); IIRS → Dehradun (not Hyderabad).
14-105.t: Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) is Hyderabad; Remote Sensing Institute (IIRS) is Dehradun.

14-107.r: VSSC, Trivandrum → research in rocket propellants and development of satellite launch vehicles; ISRO itself was established in 1969.

14-108.r: PraVaHa → ISRO's Computational Fluid Dynamics software, made by VSSC, Thiruvananthapuram, for aerodynamic design of launch and re-entry vehicles → both statements correct.
